slides.title: Chunking / [transcripts]
slides.hook: Your support-call RAG returns the customer's question and ranks the agent's answer second. Chunk by exchange: each question with its reply, speaker and timestamp on every line.
inside: Where a size split parts a question from its answer
Exchange chunks: the question with its reply
Long answers: the question on every piece
Speakers, timestamps, and when to move on

slides.title: The exchange / is the [unit]
slides.text: A transcript answers by exchange: one person asks, another replies. A line often needs its speaker to make sense.

steps: Parse each line into timestamp, speaker and text.
Start a new chunk at each turn by the asker, here the customer.
Keep the replies with it until the next question.
Exchange over the limit: split the reply at sentences, with the question line on top of each piece.
Keep speaker and timestamp on every line, and store them as metadata.

slides.title: The question / loses its [answer]
slides.text: LangChain's `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`, `chunk_size=300`, no overlap, on a sample support call, one turn per line:

visuals.label: End of chunk 3 of 6
Start of chunk 4 of 6 (wrapped)
visuals.code:
[00:59] Agent: Your workspace stays
read-only for 30 days, so you can
export everything. Go to Settings,
then Data, then Export...

slides.after: The splitter packs turns up to 300 characters. The 00:59 reply alone is longer than 300, so the question closes chunk 3 and the reply starts chunk 4.

slides.title: Search finds / the [question]
slides.text: BM25 keyword search (`rank_bm25`) over each set of chunks. Query: "What happens to our files after we cancel?"

options.output: Top hit: chunk 3, ends at the question
Top hit: question + !!its files are deleted!!

slides.after: The first top hit ends at the question mark. With exchange chunks, both pieces of the answer rank first and second.

slides.title: A long turn / drops its [speaker]
slides.text: The 00:59 answer runs past 300 characters, so the splitter fell back to spaces. Chunk 5 of 6 in full:
bullets: 19 characters: no speaker, no timestamp, nothing it refers to.
Query "Can you restore our files after we cancel?" ranks it first.
The model reads "can't restore them" with no subject and no speaker.

slides.title: Group the / [exchange]
slides.text: Start a new chunk at each customer turn (the asker), and let the agent's replies join it. One turn per line first:

visuals.label: Exchange chunk 4 of 7 (wrapped)
visuals.code:
{{[00:41] Customer:}} We renewed in March,
so that works. How long does the
refund take?
{{[00:47] Agent:}} It goes back to the
original card in 5 to 10 business days.

bullets: Group by the asker's turns: a chunk per turn would split each question from its reply again.
Every line keeps its speaker label and timestamp.
Sizes here: 47 to 285 characters, under the 300 limit.

slides.title: Repeat the / [question]
slides.text: The files exchange runs over 300 characters. Split the answer at sentences and put the question line on each piece:

visuals.label: Exchange chunk 6 of 7 (wrapped)

slides.after: Each piece of the answer carries the question it answers, so either piece can be retrieved alone.

slides.title: Keep the / [timestamps]
slides.text: The labels on each line double as metadata. Pull them out at indexing time:
bullets: Link each hit to its moment in the recording: 00:55.
Filter by speaker when the question is what the customer said.
Many meetings have no single asker. Test other rules, like a turn ending in "?", on your own calls.

cards.title: Use it when
items: Questions ask what someone said or agreed

cards.title: Move on when
items: No speaker labels: diarize the audio first, or chunk by size
Questions cover the whole meeting: summaries per topic
Topics drift inside one long turn: semantic chunking

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: Chunking at 300? Check the longest single turn first
Pick the asker per transcript type: customer, interviewer, host
Speaker label and timestamp on every line
Long answer: every piece carries its question
Store start time and speakers; link hits to the recording
No speaker labels: diarize the audio first

slides.line: An exchange chunk still leaves out which workspace and which plan the call is about. Next: prepend a short context to each chunk before embedding.
